newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSIGHT -NZ dlr breaks down to new 18-month low.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -NZ dlr breaks down to new 18-month low.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar broke down to a new 18-month low in late Wednesday morning trade as bearish sentiment continued to take its toll on the currency.
The kiwi traded to a low of US$0.6578 before recovering to 0.6582/89 at noon.
The last time the kiwi was down at these levels was January 11, 1996, when it reached an intra-day low of 0.6569.
The Trade-Weighted Index was 41 points below its Tuesday closing level by noon, at 65.44, after trading as low as 65.33.
"There was a large selling interest this morning around the 0.6620 level," a Wellington senior dealer said.
"It's just a general malaise from the last few days really. There continues to be a lack of support for the kiwi. There's no real buying interest and we continue to see sellers on any rally."
The dealer said 0.6580 was a critical level, and if the kiwi held above that it could bounce back up to the 0.6620-30 area.
However, if it made a clean break through 0.6580, charts suggested 0.6250 was the next technical objective.
